## Historical audit: H0007

**Scope.** Student trace, chunk 4 of 5 only. Original file for all event citations: `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-baseline-run/runs/baseline_ds1017_textual_a1_vm8_20261120_r1/infer_logs/textual-kitty-key-phases/turn_1/trajs.json`. Bracketed ranges below are character offsets within the cited observation, not source-code offsets.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Inferred goal | The visible work and student’s discussion indicate a Textual Kitty keyboard-protocol task involving key phases, metadata, text and shortcut compatibility. The original task instruction is not visible here; this is an inference, not a complete specification (main_agent events 159, 165, 168). |
| Actual changes | A successful edit changed `App._on_key` to check key-event aliases; the diff also shows alias checks for priority bindings (events 150 [0,188106), 185). The parser diff handles phases, modifiers, alternate keys, associated text and legacy Alt fallback (event 167). Later successful edits retain a base-key form for multi-character text and modified text (events 191, 197). An example logging phase and character was created and then edited (events 153, 233). Working-tree status showed three modified source files and an untracked example (event 224). |
| Visible validation | Imports and compilation completed without output (events 155–157). Four core test files reported **89 passed, 1 xfailed** (events 156, 158). Custom parser/API assertions passed, and a headless app test reported a shifted alias binding worked (events 160–161, 163–164). A later shift-text probe showed `shift+a`, character `A`, and relevant metadata (events 199–200). Formatting checks passed after parser edits (events 220–221). |
| Interruption and failures | The broader non-snapshot run timed out to background at roughly 16% and was deliberately stopped (events 187–188, 194, 205–206). A later key/input/text-area run timed out to background; by 69% its output showed failure markers, and the student sent SIGINT to obtain details. The provided chunk ends before those details or a final result (events 208–209, 239–244). A proposed sleep command was separately blocked; that is not evidence of a test failure (event 227). |
| Teacher and exploration | No delivered teacher text or adoption evidence appears in this chunk. The linked system-prompt archive in the inventory establishes availability, not receipt. The student independently probed Alt fallback variants, searched documentation and considered compatibility; notably ESC+DEL produced `ctrl+w`, while ESC+backspace produced `alt+backspace` (events 169–173). |

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Inventory metadata reports formal status **solved**, with 23/23 fail-to-pass and 57/57 pass-to-pass tests; the underlying evaluation output is not visible in this chunk. Thus the reported formal success coexists with an incomplete visible broader run containing unexplained failure markers. Neither their cause nor the final patch’s complete behavior can be established from this excerpt.

**Lessons.** Transferably, targeted assertions and integration checks provide different evidence from a broad suite, and an interrupted run cannot be counted as passing. Task-specific unresolved hypotheses include legacy ESC+DEL compatibility and the cause of the input/text-area failures; the student’s speculation is not a diagnosis. This is a code task, not a scene audit.
